l.i: Captúsque grandi munere mittiturAugusta sacra limina qui domusPerrupit audax, & retectoEnse tuum latus appetiuit.Hac arte Princeps concidit Auricus,Quo dura fortes vindice vinculaRupere Belga, quum TyrannusIussit Iber violare leges,Iurata Genti fœdera subruens.Hæc Roma monstrat perfida, quæ fidemPactámque dextram ChristianisFraude noua temerare sancit.Cur pace s:cla, Tygride seuior,Heu Roma quæris sub iuga mittereHispana bellaces Britannos,Innocuúmque caput fatigas?Vrit profanos fœmina PræsulesDilecta calo, cui placet obsequiChristo docenti: cuíque cordi estArdua cum pietate Virtus.Vrit cruentis quod cruciatibusDulcem coactos linquere PatriamSolatur, & Christum sequutosHospitiis recreat benignis.Quòd fida sacros auxiliis gregesFirmat piorum non trepidantibus.Longósque Belgarum laboresMarte potens miserata sanat.

page.notes: Catchword "Quod" is printed at lower right, outside the text block. Long s rendered as plain s. Page is verse; the lines are shown with line breaks inside one paragraph. Some letters in the first line ("Captúsque") and "s:cla" line are doubtful.
